aa1bc1.io: Summarize side effects and toxic manifestations of antiarrhythmic drugs
aa1bc1.q: Which drug lists agranulocytosis among its toxicities?
opts: Correct. Propafenone's toxicity list includes agranulocytosis, anemia and thrombocytopenia.
Flecainide's blood toxicity is thrombocytopenia, not agranulocytosis; propafenone lists agranulocytosis.
Lidocaine's toxicity is in the central nervous system, with hypersensitivity; propafenone lists agranulocytosis.
Disopyramide's toxicity is hypotension, antimuscarinic effects, conduction disturbances, heart failure and torsades; propafenone lists agranulocytosis.

aa1bc1.io: Describe absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion of antiarrhythmic drugs
opts: Correct. Lidocaine undergoes extensive first-pass metabolism, so it is given intravenously rather than by mouth.
A 40-day half-life belongs to amiodarone, which needs loading doses; lidocaine is intravenous because of extensive first-pass metabolism.
Elimination unchanged by the kidneys is listed for dofetilide; lidocaine is given intravenously because of extensive first-pass metabolism.
A duration of action of 3 to 4 hours
A 3 to 4 hour duration is procainamide's, solved with a slow-release preparation; lidocaine is intravenous because of first-pass metabolism.

aa1bc1.io: Summarize side effects and toxic manifestations of antiarrhythmic drugs
aa1bc1.q: Which arrhythmia can flecainide cause that resists treatment?
opts: Supraventricular arrhythmias are among flecainide's indications; the arrhythmia it can cause that resists treatment is ventricular tachycardia.
Bradycardia is listed for propafenone, through its beta-blocking activity; flecainide's treatment-resistant arrhythmia is ventricular tachycardia.
Correct. Flecainide's toxicity list includes ventricular tachycardia resistant to treatment, a form of the proarrhythmia every antiarrhythmic can cause.
Heart block is listed for propranolol and digoxin; flecainide's treatment-resistant arrhythmia is ventricular tachycardia.

aa1bc1.io: Describe adverse effects of antiarrhythmic drugs
aa1bc1.q: Which respiratory effect of flecainide matters in a patient with asthma?
opts: Pneumonitis, with pulmonary fibrosis, is amiodarone's lung toxicity; flecainide's respiratory effect is bronchospasm.
Respiratory paralysis is listed for magnesium sulfate; flecainide's respiratory effect is bronchospasm.
Pulmonary fibrosis (potentially fatal) is amiodarone's; flecainide's respiratory effect is bronchospasm.
Correct. Bronchospasm is on flecainide's toxicity list (and propafenone's), a concern in asthma.

aa1bc1.io: Summarize side effects and toxic manifestations of antiarrhythmic drugs
aa1bc1.q: Which cardiac effect is on lidocaine's toxicity list?
opts: Slowing of atrioventricular conduction (up to heart block) belongs to beta blockers, class IV and digoxin; lidocaine's list says it increases atrioventricular conduction.
Correct. Lidocaine's toxicity list includes increased atrioventricular conduction, along with hypersensitivity and its central nervous system effects.
Torsades de pointes belongs to class IA, dofetilide and sotalol; lidocaine's cardiac toxicity is increased atrioventricular conduction.
Decreased contractility is disopyramide's (heart failure); lidocaine's listed cardiac toxicity is increased atrioventricular conduction.

aa1bc1.io: Identify antiarrhythmic drug classes and commonly prescribed antiarrhythmic drugs
aa1bc1.q: Which drug is a class IC antiarrhythmic?
opts: Correct. Flecainide is class IC (propafenone is the other); it blocks sodium and potassium channels in the ventricles.
Lidocaine is the class IB drug, working mainly in ischemic tissue; flecainide is class IC.
Quinidine is class IA, the D-isomer of quinine; flecainide is class IC.
Sotalol is a beta blocker with class III potassium channel action; flecainide is class IC.

aa1bc1.q: Why is propafenone a concern in a patient with heart failure?
opts: Raising digoxin levels is amiodarone's listed interaction; propafenone's concern in heart failure is that it can worsen it.
Correct. Propafenone can worsen congestive heart failure, an effect of its beta-blocking activity.
Increased atrioventricular conduction is on lidocaine's toxicity list; propafenone's concern in heart failure is that it can worsen it.
A lupus-like syndrome is procainamide's effect; propafenone's concern in heart failure is that it can worsen it.

aa1bc1.io: Identify antiarrhythmic drug classes and commonly prescribed antiarrhythmic drugs
aa1bc1.q: Which drug is the class IB antiarrhythmic?
opts: Flecainide is class IC, which affects the normal heart and markedly slows phase 0; the class IB drug is lidocaine.
Procainamide is class IA, with an active metabolite that has class III activity; the class IB drug is lidocaine.
Propafenone is class IC with added beta-blocking activity; the class IB drug is lidocaine.
Correct. Lidocaine is the class IB sodium channel blocker; it works mainly on sodium channels in ischemic tissue.

aa1bc1.io: Identify indications for commonly used antiarrhythmic drugs
aa1bc1.q: Which setting is a listed indication for lidocaine?
opts: Lidocaine is not effective against atrial arrhythmias; its listed settings are ventricular arrhythmias and acute myocardial infarction.
ruled out by a stated finding
Torsades de pointes is treated with intravenous magnesium sulfate; lidocaine is listed for ventricular arrhythmias and acute myocardial infarction.
Correct. Lidocaine is listed for ventricular tachycardia and premature beats, ventricular fibrillation and acute myocardial infarction, where ischemic tissue is its target.
Paroxysmal supraventricular tachycardia is the indication for adenosine and for verapamil or diltiazem; lidocaine's are ventricular arrhythmias and acute myocardial infarction.

aa1bc1.io: Describe the molecular mechanism of action of antiarrhythmic drugs
aa1bc1.q: Where do class IB drugs have their greatest effect?
opts: Affecting the normal heart is the class IC feature; class IB has little effect in normal tissue and works mainly in ischemic tissue.
Lidocaine is not effective against atrial arrhythmias; class IB works mainly in ischemic tissue.
ruled out by a stated finding
Correct. Class IB drugs have a higher affinity in ischemic tissue and little effect in normal tissue; lidocaine is most effective on sodium channels in ischemic tissue.
Suppressing the sinoatrial node is a class IV action (verapamil, diltiazem); class IB works mainly in ischemic tissue.

aa1bc1.io: Identify indications for commonly used antiarrhythmic drugs
aa1bc1.q: Which arrhythmia is a listed indication for flecainide?
opts: Torsades de pointes is treated with intravenous magnesium sulfate; flecainide is listed for life-threatening sustained ventricular arrhythmias.
Correct. Flecainide is listed for life-threatening sustained ventricular arrhythmias and supraventricular arrhythmias, in patients without significant structural heart damage.
Flecainide increases mortality in myocardial infarction; lidocaine is the drug listed for acute myocardial infarction.
ruled out by a stated finding
Slowing the ventricular rate is digoxin's listed indication; flecainide is listed for life-threatening sustained ventricular arrhythmias.

aa1bc1.io: Identify indications for commonly used antiarrhythmic drugs
aa1bc1.q: Lidocaine is ineffective against which type of arrhythmia?
opts: Ventricular tachycardia and premature beats are listed indications for lidocaine; it is atrial arrhythmias that it does not treat.
Ventricular fibrillation is a listed indication for lidocaine; it is not effective against atrial arrhythmias.
Premature beats are listed with ventricular tachycardia among lidocaine's indications; lidocaine is not effective against atrial arrhythmias.
Correct. Lidocaine works on sodium channels in ischemic tissue, has less effect on normal tissue, and is not effective against atrial arrhythmias.

aa1bc1.io: Describe absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion of antiarrhythmic drugs
aa1bc1.q: Which pharmacokinetic feature is listed for flecainide?
opts: Extensive first-pass metabolism is why lidocaine must be given intravenously; flecainide has a long 14-hour half-life and is also oral.
Correct. Flecainide has a long half-life (14 hours) and can be given by mouth or intravenously.
A 10-second half-life belongs to adenosine; flecainide's half-life is a long 14 hours.
Elimination unchanged by the kidneys is listed for dofetilide; flecainide's listed feature is a long 14-hour half-life.

aa1bc1.io: Describe the molecular mechanism of action of antiarrhythmic drugs
aa1bc1.q: Which feature separates class IC from class IB?
opts: IC works mainly in ischemic tissue
Working mainly in ischemic tissue is the class IB feature, the reverse of class IC, which affects the normal heart.
Shortening phase 3 is the class IB action; class IC slows phase 0 and prolongs the refractory period.
Correct. Class IC slows phase 0 and conduction, prolongs the refractory period and affects the normal heart; class IB has little effect on normal tissue.
Blocking L-type calcium channels is the class IV mechanism; class IC drugs are sodium channel blockers that affect the normal heart.

aa1bc2.q: Which history is a listed contraindication to lidocaine?
opts: Glaucoma contraindicates disopyramide because of its anticholinergic action; lidocaine's listed contraindication is seizures.
Heart block contraindicates disopyramide and is a toxicity of propranolol and digoxin; lidocaine's listed contraindication is seizures.
Correct. Seizures are a listed contraindication to lidocaine, whose own central nervous system toxicity can end in seizures.
Asthma matters for bronchospasm with propranolol, sotalol and the class IC drugs; lidocaine's listed contraindication is seizures.

aa1bc2.io: Describe the molecular mechanism of action of antiarrhythmic drugs
aa1bc2.q: Which automaticity do class IB drugs decrease?
opts: Correct. Class IB drugs shorten phase 3 and decrease ectopic foci automaticity.
Suppressing the sinoatrial node is listed for verapamil and diltiazem (class IV); class IB decreases ectopic foci automaticity.
Lidocaine is not effective against atrial arrhythmias; class IB decreases the automaticity of ectopic foci.
ruled out by a stated finding
Slowing the atrioventricular node is what class II and class IV drugs do; class IB decreases ectopic foci automaticity.

aa1bc2.io: Describe the molecular mechanism of action of antiarrhythmic drugs
aa1bc2.q: Which change in the action potential is most marked with class IC drugs?
opts: A shortened phase 3 is the class IB picture; class IC markedly slows phase 0.
A prolonged phase 3 with an unchanged upstroke is the class III picture; class IC markedly slows phase 0.
Correct. The class IC tracing shows a markedly slower phase 0 upstroke; class IC slows phase 0 and conduction and prolongs the refractory period.
A flatter phase 4 in pacemaker cells is the class II and class IV picture; class IC markedly slows phase 0.

aa1bc2.io: Summarize side effects and toxic manifestations of antiarrhythmic drugs
aa1bc2.q: Which serious risk is listed for flecainide after a myocardial infarction?
opts: Pneumonitis and pulmonary fibrosis (potentially fatal) belong to amiodarone; flecainide's listed risk after infarction is increased mortality.
Correct. Flecainide's toxicity list includes increased mortality in myocardial infarction, which is why it is kept for hearts without significant structural damage.
A lupus-like syndrome is procainamide's effect, more often in slow acetylators; flecainide's risk after infarction is increased mortality.
Cinchonism is quinidine's tinnitus, dizziness and blurred vision; flecainide's risk after infarction is increased mortality.

aa1bc2.io: Describe the molecular mechanism of action of antiarrhythmic drugs
aa1bc2.q: Propafenone shares flecainide's mechanism and adds which activity?
opts: Alpha blockade at higher doses is quinidine's indirect action; propafenone adds beta-blocking activity.
Activating atrial potassium channels is adenosine's action; propafenone adds beta-blocking activity.
Calcium channel blockade is the class IV mechanism (amiodarone also has it); propafenone adds beta-blocking activity.
Correct. Propafenone has the same mechanism as flecainide plus beta-blocking activity, which brings bradycardia, bronchospasm and worse heart failure.

aa1bc2.io: Describe the molecular mechanism of action of antiarrhythmic drugs
aa1bc2.q: Which electrocardiogram intervals does flecainide prolong?
opts: Flecainide prolongs the PR and QRS intervals but also the QT interval; all three lengthen.
Correct. Flecainide prolongs the PR, QRS and QT intervals; it blocks both sodium and potassium channels in the ventricles.
Flecainide prolongs the QRS and QT intervals but also the PR interval; all three lengthen.
Flecainide prolongs the PR and QT intervals but also the QRS interval; all three lengthen.

aa1bc2.io: Describe the molecular mechanism of action of antiarrhythmic drugs
aa1bc2.q: Which effect on the cardiac action potential defines class IB?
opts: A markedly slowed phase 0 is the class IC picture; class IB leaves the upstroke alone and shortens phase 3.
A prolonged phase 3 is the class III action (potassium channel block), the reverse of class IB, which shortens phase 3.
A flatter phase 4 in pacemaker cells is the class II and class IV picture; class IB shortens phase 3 in working muscle.
Correct. Class IB shortens phase 3, so the action potential ends sooner, with an unchanged upstroke; it also decreases ectopic foci automaticity.

aa1bc2.io: Describe adverse effects of antiarrhythmic drugs
aa1bc2.q: Which adverse effect of propafenone comes from its beta-blocking activity?
opts: Agranulocytosis, with anemia and thrombocytopenia, is on propafenone's list but is not a beta-blocking effect; bronchospasm is.
Blurred vision and dizziness are on propafenone's list but do not come from beta blockade; bronchospasm does.
Correct. Propafenone's toxicity list pairs bronchospasm with beta-adrenergic blockade; bradycardia and worsening heart failure come from the same activity.
Propafenone is proarrhythmic like every antiarrhythmic, but that is not a beta-blocking effect; bronchospasm is.

aa1bc2.io: Summarize side effects and toxic manifestations of antiarrhythmic drugs
aa1bc2.q: Lidocaine toxicity shows mainly in which system?
opts: Correct. Lidocaine's toxicity is central nervous system toxicity: drowsiness, confusion, restlessness, muscle twitches, seizures, and nystagmus as the early sign.
Pneumonitis and pulmonary fibrosis are amiodarone's lung toxicity; lidocaine's toxicity is in the central nervous system.
Thyroid abnormalities belong to amiodarone, an analog of thyroid hormone; lidocaine's toxicity is in the central nervous system.
Bone marrow suppression is listed for procainamide; lidocaine's toxicity is in the central nervous system.

aa1bc2.q: Flecainide is to be used only in which patients?
opts: Correct. Flecainide is to be used only in patients without significant structural damage to the heart, and it increases mortality after myocardial infarction.
Those with a prior myocardial infarction
Flecainide increases mortality after myocardial infarction, so this is the reverse of who should get it.
Depressed function is a damaged heart, and flecainide is limited to hearts without significant structural damage.
Acetylator status matters for procainamide's lupus-like syndrome; flecainide's restriction is no significant structural heart damage.

aa1bc2.io: Summarize side effects and toxic manifestations of antiarrhythmic drugs
aa1bc2.q: Which nervous system effects are listed for flecainide?
opts: Tinnitus and dizziness with blurred vision make up quinidine's cinchonism; flecainide's listed effects are blurred vision and tremor.
Nystagmus and muscle twitches are lidocaine's central nervous system toxicity; flecainide's are blurred vision and tremor.
Neuropathy, muscle weakness and ataxia belong to amiodarone; flecainide's listed effects are blurred vision and tremor.
Correct. Flecainide's toxicity list starts with blurred vision and tremor, and also includes seizures.

aa1bc2.io: Describe the molecular mechanism of action of antiarrhythmic drugs
aa1bc2.q: Besides sodium channels, which channels does flecainide block in the ventricles?
opts: L-type calcium channels are blocked by the class IV drugs verapamil and diltiazem; flecainide adds potassium channel block.
Beta-blocking activity is what propafenone adds to the shared class IC mechanism; flecainide's second target is the potassium channel.
Alpha blockade at higher doses is quinidine's indirect action; flecainide's second target is the potassium channel.
Correct. Flecainide blocks sodium and potassium channels in the ventricles and slows recovery of the sodium channel.

aa1bc2.io: Summarize side effects and toxic manifestations of antiarrhythmic drugs
aa1bc2.q: Which finding is an early sign of lidocaine toxicity?
opts: Seizures are part of lidocaine's central nervous system toxicity, but the finding listed as the early sign is nystagmus.
Correct. Nystagmus is listed as the early sign of lidocaine toxicity, within its central nervous system toxicity.
Tinnitus, with dizziness and blurred vision, is quinidine's cinchonism; the early sign of lidocaine toxicity is nystagmus.
Corneal deposits are an adverse effect of amiodarone; the early sign of lidocaine toxicity is nystagmus.
